sections.title: Minimum quotations
sections.summary: Purchases above 500000 AOA require two quotations. Supplied as a one-line statement in chat on 2026-09-21; the policy document, its version, effective date and section numbering were not supplied.

sections.title: Legal basis cited
sections.summary: The template cites Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD, Brazil). The organization operates in Angola; the citation is a jurisdiction mismatch and is not adopted as a requirement source. The template itself was not supplied.

sources.title: Purchase case P1 — 600000 AOA, one quotation

sections.title: Case P1
sections.summary: Amount 600000 AOA; one quotation on record. Stated in chat on 2026-09-21; no export, case id, dates, requester, approver or attachments were supplied.

decisions.question: P1 (600000 AOA) has one quotation on record where the policy requires two. Was a second quotation obtained and not attached, or was a documented exception approved? If neither, who decides the remediation for P1 (obtain the second quotation, record a justified single-source exception, or record the deviation)?

Confirm the policy wording, version and effective date: is the 500000 AOA threshold 'above' (strictly greater) or 'from', and is it measured on the amount with or without tax? Does the policy admit single-source exceptions and, if so, who approves them?

The consultant template cites Brazilian LGPD for an Angolan process. Replace the citation with the applicable Angolan data-protection instrument, verified against https://apd.ao/ao/legislacao/ (instrument, article, status, verification date), or remove the legal citation from the template. Who owns the corrected template?

The two-quotation control is not yet mapped to a Provia workflow because no workflow design or manifest was supplied. Should the purchasing workflow be designed (or the existing one exported) so that the quotation check becomes a named action with evidence, and who owns that design?
